Obbe Vermeij, ancien directeur technique de Rockstar North, pense que la sortie de GTA VI sur PC pourrait arriver plus tôt que prévu. Selon lui, Rockstar et Take-Two pourraient vouloir devancer toute tentative de version non officielle vibe-codée à l’aide d’outils d’IA.
Obbe Vermeij a quitté le studio en 2009 et reconnaît ne pas savoir ce que l’éditeur a en tête. C’est donc maintenant un observateur de l’industrie de l’IA qui parle, pas un employé qui connaît les plans de Rockstar Games. Il considère que l’IA générative a profondément changé la donne et que la question se pose désormais aux développeurs comme aux éditeurs : comment éviter que leurs jeux soient dupliqués par des chatbots et ainsi, qu’une version non officielle devance la version officielle déjà prévue ?
Dans un entretien accordé à nos confrères de Rock Paper Shotgun , il rappelle que la plupart des éditeurs préfèrent lancer un jeu sur toutes les plateformes en même temps, ce qui ne nécessite qu’une seule campagne marketing. Rockstar fait un autre choix : la série Grand Theft Auto sort d’abord sur console , ensuite, elle sortira sur PC, probablement. Mais selon lui, les versions adaptées avec l’aide de l’IA compliquent le maintien de ces sorties majeures aux exclusivités console.
Vermeij ne cache pas les limites d’une telle tentative. Adapter GTA VI sur ordinateur par ce moyen consommerait énormément de tokens et donnerait probablement des performances moindres qu’un portage natif dans les règles de l’art. Le projet demanderait aussi beaucoup de temps et vraisemblablement plusieurs dizaines de milliers de dollars .
Malgré tout cela, selon lui, quelqu’un va essayer. Cette menace pourrait justement, selon lui, inciter Rockstar à s’activer sérieusement pour la version PC. L’IA générative est efficace pour traiter de grandes bases de code existantes, ainsi, une version PC officielle pourrait arriver un peu plus tôt qu’on ne l’imaginait. Dans tous les cas, l’éditeur fera son maximum pour éviter qu’une version non officielle ne se retrouve entre les mains des joueurs.
L’ancien directeur technique va au-delà du cas de GTA VI. Il voit dans l’IA générative une menace existentielle pour les développeurs. Qu’il s’agisse de grands éditeurs ou de petits studios indépendants, comme le sien, GabberGames, qui sont encore plus vulnérables.
Cependant, selon lui, un groupe comme Take-Two peut mobiliser ses avocats contre toute tentative de décompilation, et un jeu de cette taille, plus de 200 Go tout de même, pourrait être trop complexe pour être bien géré par une IA. Il admet pourtant ne pas voir comment s’en protéger complètement. Il parle d’un « nouveau monde » et estime que les deux prochaines années montreront comment la situation évoluera.

articles.t: 'GTA 6' Runs Best on PlayStation 5 Consoles | Lifehacker
articles.chapeau: Rockstar confirmed that some consoles will play GTA 6 better than others. But there's one console that runs the game best.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5 , and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.
Now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6 —unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.
Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday , which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.
No matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar says that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.
To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro."
PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.
While PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.
In the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.
That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar says that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.
Again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6 , so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying . But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the company hasn't explained why that is.

articles.t: GTA 6 pre-order guide: All exclusive content and pre-order bonuses
articles.chapeau: This guide lists all of the exclusive content you can grab by pre-ordering either of GTA 6's versions, including every cosmetic in the Ultimate Edition.
articles.txt:
With GTA 6 right around the corner, you're probably wondering if it's worth it to pre-order. After all, if you don't, you can check the reviews post-launch and decide whether it's worth splashing your hard-earned cash. One thing worth taking into account though is pre-order bonuses, which GTA 6 does have a few of.
If you're weighing up whether it's worth jumping on your purchase early, we've listed all of the GTA 6 pre-order bonuses below , as well as a refresh on what exclusive content comes with its Ultimate Edition so you have all the info before you buy.
For pre-ordering either version of Grand Theft Auto 6, you'll get two pre-order bonuses: the Vintage Vice City Pack and a free month of GTA+ .
The main event here is definitely the Vintage Vice City Pack, which seems to be a callback to the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City . You'll get a few different cosmetics and items, with the pack including:
As for the GTA+ trial, this is just a free month of Rockstar's GTA Online membership. After becoming a member, you can redeem some free cash, nab exclusive vehicles, purchase items at heavy discounts, and reap some other benefits. So if you want to pop back into GTA Online and rinse it of all its worth before GTA 6's online mode inevitably hits stores, this could be a big boon.
The other bonus of pre-ordering is the ability to pre-load the game . GTA 6 is going to be 210 GB in size , so being able to tackle that hefty download in the lead-up to launch will save you a bunch of time and let you get stuck in the moment it drops.
When you're going to pre-order the game, the big question will be whether you buy the standard edition or splash more cash to get the added Ultimate Edition benefits. Both versions include the pre-order bonuses mentioned above, but the Ultimate Edition adds a stack of exclusive content to redeem. Really, what you choose is up to you, but let's recap what you get in the GTA 6: Ultimate Edition so you can make your call ahead of time.
That's a whole heap of stuff that won't be in the standard edition of the game, so if you want some exclusive cars, a few new missions and a bunch of shops not accessible in the base game, it could be worth the extra dough. At the end of the day though, that's up to you! It seems like the game's going to be full of cosmetics and activities as is.
With that, you know all the exclusive content you'll get by pre-ordering GTA 6 and buying the Ultimate Edition. Are you planning to pre-order the game? Let us know! If you are, then check out our guides on how to preload GTA 6 and when it will launch on your console . If you're looking for something a little different though, you can always find our full list of GTA 6 guides here .

articles.t: GTA 6 : Une nouvelle bande-annonce de préchargement semble lancer une pique aux fans critiques
articles.chapeau: Le préchargement de GTA 6 a enfin commencé, et Rockstar a publié une nouvelle bande-annonce courte pour marquer l’occasion. Si ces images offrent peu de matière à spéculer, certains fans pensent que Rockstar cherchait à faire passer un message.
articles.txt:
Les fans peuvent précharger GTA 6 depuis le 10 novembre. Rockstar a également publié une nouvelle bande-annonce pour l'occasion (intégrée ci-dessous), et un passage en particulier a suscité un vif débat. Pour comprendre pourquoi, il vaut la peine de revenir sur l'Extended Look publié fin août. À 17:22 , Jason effectue un salto arrière pour plonger dans l'eau. Cependant, il ne commence sa rotation qu'une fois déjà en l'air. Cela n'a pas beaucoup de sens du point de vue de la physique, et de nombreux spectateurs ont trouvé l'animation peu naturelle. Rockstar a donc essuyé quelques critiques.
La bande-annonce de préchargement de 30 secondes s'ouvre sur une brève scène en boîte de nuit avant de montrer un pilote de course exécutant un salto arrière à la perfection – et c'est sur ce passage que les fans se sont attardés. De nombreux internautes sur Reddit soupçonnent Rockstar d'avoir délibérément inclus cette acrobatie en guise de réponse malicieuse à ceux qui avaient critiqué l'animation de Jason, presque comme pour dire que le studio sait parfaitement animer des mouvements acrobatiques. " Ils savaient EXACTEMENT ce qu'ils faisaient avec ce salto arrière ", peut-on lire dans le commentaire ayant reçu le plus de votes positifs lors d'une récente discussion au sein de la communauté. Impossible de dire si ce salto arrière était réellement destiné à lancer une pique aux détracteurs. C'est néanmoins ainsi que de nombreux fans l'ont interprété.
Il existe également une distinction importante : le salto arrière de Jason dans l'Extended Look semble provenir d'une séquence de gameplay, tandis que l'acrobatie de la bande-annonce de préchargement ressemble davantage à une séquence scriptée. Si Rockstar voulait vraiment faire passer un message, un salto arrière tout aussi convaincant en pleine phase de jeu dans GTA 6 ( disponible en précommande sur Amazon ) serait un argument plus solide.

articles.t: Liberty City dans GTA 6 ? Une nouvelle bande-annonce ravive l’espoir d’une deuxième ville
articles.chapeau: Un petit détail dans la nouvelle bande-annonce de préchargement de GTA 6 a relancé les spéculations sur la présence de lieux supplémentaires dans le jeu. Certains fans espèrent même que Liberty City pourrait faire son apparition en tant que deuxième ville jouable.
articles.txt:
Au premier abord, la nouvelle bande-annonce de préchargement de GTA 6 semblait n'offrir guère plus qu'une possible pique aux fans qui avaient critiqué une précédente animation de salto arrière . Mais un autre détail a désormais attiré l'attention des fans. Cette fois, les regards se portent sur un yacht qui apparaît aux alentours de la dixième seconde . Sur sa poupe, sous le nom "Ships And Giggles", figure le mot "Gloriana".
Cette inscription, à elle seule, ne révèle pas grand-chose. Mais une publication du créateur de contenu TGG , spécialisé dans GTA , a lancé une discussion sur une éventuelle deuxième carte. TGG a partagé une image du yacht sur X, accompagnée d'un vêtement qu'il a décrit comme un "t-shirt Liberty City". Il a également fait remarquer, sur un ton apparemment sarcastique, que ces détails n'étaient sûrement là que pour étoffer l'univers du jeu. Son commentaire semble suggérer que Rockstar pourrait faire allusion à des lieux situés au-delà du cadre connu du jeu.
Ce que TGG pense précisément que l'inscription sur le yacht pourrait révéler reste flou. Certains utilisateurs de X jugent néanmoins plausible l'idée de lieux supplémentaires et supposent que "Gloriana" pourrait désigner un autre État – peut-être une version fictive de la Géorgie imaginée par Rockstar. Le supposé "t-shirt Liberty City" laisse toutefois les fans perplexes, car il ne présente aucun lien évident avec la ville.
Les spéculations vont encore plus loin dans les réponses à la publication de TGG. L'utilisateur de X Blue Thunder affirme être certain à 95% que Liberty City apparaîtra comme deuxième carte dans GTA 6 . Selon sa théorie, la métropole bien connue des joueurs de GTA 4 deviendrait accessible vers le milieu de la campagne. Il n'apporte toutefois aucune preuve concrète à l'appui de cette affirmation.
La théorie a suscité des espoirs sur Reddit , même si elle semble aussi assez tirée par les cheveux. Blue Thunder ne fournit aucune preuve pour étayer sa prédiction, et le chiffre de 95% n’est que son estimation personnelle. On devrait savoir d’ici quelques jours si GTA 6 ( disponible en précommande sur Amazon ) propose réellement des villes ou des États supplémentaires.

articles.t: GTA 6 : voici pourquoi les 30 FPS sur PS5 et les consoles Xbox Series pourraient décevoir les joueurs
articles.chapeau: Rockstar a récemment dévoilé le profil de performances de GTA 6 sur les consoles Sony PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro et Xbox Series X | S. Le jeu est limité à une fréquence d’images bien inférieure à celle qu’espéraient de nombreux joueurs. Hardware Unboxed, spécialiste chevronné des tests de matériel, explique pourquoi cela pourrait nuire à l’expérience de jeu.
articles.txt:
Rockstar a révélé que GTA 6 tourne à une cadence verrouillée à 30 FPS sur la Sony PS5 et les consoles Xbox Series. Hardware Unboxed, spécialiste chevronné des tests, estime que, si les 30 FPS sont un compromis consenti par le studio pour maintenir une qualité graphique élevée, cette faible fréquence d’images pose un problème majeur. HU explique que les 30 FPS de GTA 6 posent problème tant du point de vue de la qualité visuelle que de celui du gameplay.
Du point de vue de la qualité visuelle, les 30 FPS offrent un rendu « plus flou sur les écrans modernes, et moins fluide », selon HU. Les dalles OLED et LCD modernes sont très réactives et passent d’une image à la suivante presque instantanément. À 30 FPS, chaque image reste affichée à l’écran pendant 33,33 ms avant que l’écran ne passe à la suivante. Le résultat est assez désagréable à regarder. Les développeurs utilisent donc un flou de mouvement prononcé pour masquer et adoucir cette transition. Cependant, un flou de mouvement prononcé réduit la netteté des mouvements et brouille les détails visuels fins.
Il faut également tenir compte de la généralisation actuelle des écrans et des contenus à fréquence d’images élevée. Il est assez courant de trouver des dalles 120 Hz sur les smartphones modernes et les téléviseurs. La majorité des contenus sur des plateformes comme YouTube sont également tournés à 60 FPS. Les joueurs sont donc habitués à des images fluides, ce qui rend le passage à 30 FPS dans GTA 6 encore plus perceptible
Du point de vue du gameplay, une fréquence de 30 FPS signifie que le jeu sera sensiblement plus saccadé, avec une bonne dose de latence des commandes. Comme le dit HU, cela rend le gameplay « moins agréable ».
Il faut toutefois reconnaître ici que Rockstar a en quelque sorte les mains liées dans cette situation. Pour que GTA 6 soit à la hauteur des attentes des fans, Rockstar a dû créer un monde vivant peuplé de PNJ, avec des interactions dynamiques uniques, et ainsi de suite. Cela nécessite une puissance de calcul du processeur dont les consoles PS5 et Xbox Series ne disposent pas. Même la PS5 Pro doit se contenter d’un processeur peu puissant basé sur l’ancienne architecture AMD Zen 2, qui accuse quatre générations de retard sur la dernière architecture de processeur AMD .
Rockstar a donc dû prendre la décision difficile de renoncer à ses ambitions de 60 FPS au profit d’une cadence verrouillée à 30 FPS afin de garantir un monde ouvert dynamique.
S’il faudra attendre pour voir comment les joueurs accueilleront GTA 6 sur consoles, une chose est assez claire : c’est sur PC que GTA 6 offrira les meilleurs graphismes et la meilleure expérience de jeu.

articles.t: Un initié explique pourquoi GTA 6 tourne à 30 FPS même sur la Sony PlayStation 5 Pro
articles.chapeau: Grand Theft Auto 6 sortira le 19 novembre sur les consoles Sony PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro et Microsoft Xbox Series X | S. Cependant, Rockstar a annoncé que GTA 6 sera limité à 30 FPS. RedGamingTech, un initié réputé, a tenté d’expliquer la véritable raison de cette limitation à 30 FPS.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 tourne à une cadence verrouillée à 30 FPS, même sur la Sony PlayStation 5 Pro. De nombreux joueurs attribuent ce sacrifice en matière de performances à la décision de Rockstar d’utiliser le ray tracing. RedGamingTech, un initié reconnu qui était auparavant réputé pour ses fuites sur le matériel informatique, explique que si GTA 6 tourne à 30 FPS sur les consoles Sony PS5 et Xbox Series X | S, c’est davantage à cause de la lenteur de leurs processeurs que du ray tracing.
RGT écrit sur X que GTA 6 propose un monde ouvert « absolument IMMENSE », rempli de PNJ et de systèmes qui mettent les processeurs à rude épreuve. Les processeurs des PS5 et Xbox Series doivent gérer « la physique, l’IA, le code général du jeu et, oui, les threads de rendu ». Sachant que les processeurs à 8 cœurs des PS5, PS5 Pro et Xbox Series X | S reposent sur l’architecture vieillissante AMD Zen 2, GTA 6 n’est pas un jeu facile à faire tourner sur les consoles modernes.
Les processeurs peu puissants des consoles sont donc très probablement la principale raison pour laquelle Rockstar a verrouillé GTA 6 à 30 FPS sur consoles. Malheureusement, le jeu à 30 FPS offre un moins bon rendu sur les écrans modernes dont les pixels ont un temps de réponse rapide . Les joueurs qui souhaitent jouer à des fréquences de rafraîchissement plus élevées pour profiter d’images nettes, d’une expérience fluide et d’une faible latence des commandes devront attendre le portage PC de GTA 6 .
La bonne nouvelle, c’est que le portage PC de GTA 6 pourrait arriver plus tôt que prévu. Rockstar craindrait que des moddeurs utilisent l’IA pour porter la version console de GTA 6 sur PC. Cette crainte n’est pas infondée, puisque nous avons vu l’IA donner un formidable coup d’accélérateur à la scène de l’émulation de consoles . Certains ont même utilisé l’IA pour porter des jeux exclusifs à PlayStation sur PC .

articles.chapeau: Predownloads of the game began on Nov. 10. GTA 6 will take up a whopping 212 GB of console space.
articles.txt:
( NewsNation ) — We’re a few days away from the highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI , the latest installment in one of the most controversial video game series of all time.
The upcoming game comes 13 years after GTA 5 was released on the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 — two console generations ago — and GTA 5 has since been released on multiple platforms.
GTA 5 has sold over 230 million units since 2013, making it the second bestselling game in history.
After multiple delays, the game was initially scheduled for a fall 2025 release, but Rockstar, the game’s developer, confirmed GTA 6 will launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Nov. 19.
A media blitz, including multiple previews, magazine covers and a Netflix gameplay reveal , has increased the hype, and with the game just eight days away, as of the time of this writing, the chances of Rockstar delaying GTA 6 are low.
When the game was officially announced, Rockstar confirmed it would initially release on Sony and Microsoft consoles, angering PC gamers.
The company plans to release a PC version, targeting Q1 2027, according to Gamesbeat .
Grand Theft Auto’s multiplayer component, GTA Online, has been immensely popular among players and a cash cow for Rockstar.
GTA Online launched months after GTA V’s launch and has continued to grow since, earning $10 million in revenue a week, Kotaku reported in April.
Rockstar confirmed the game’s multiplayer experience won’t be released simultaneously with GTA 6, but there is a planned release.
Grand Theft Auto VI will be an all-digital release at launch. A physical version of the game is scheduled for 2027.
Rockstar confirmed earlier this year there will be an $80 standard version of GTA 6 and an ultimate edition, which will cost $100 and include additional features and perks.
Predownloads of the game began on Nov. 10. GTA 6 will take up a whopping 212 GB of console space.
Gamers will be able to explore the fictional state of Leonida — based on the very real Florida — as Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval in the open-world game.

articles.txt:
Guessing GTA 6's Metacritic score could bag you a $150, $250, or $500 gift card.
Fancy netting yourself a $500 gift card? You can do so simply by guessing what Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Metacritic score will be.
Metacritic has seemingly partnered with Fandom in order to launch a competition where soon-to-be GTA VI players can guess the game’s Metascore ahead of its release on November 19.
All you need to do to enter is head to the dedicated website set up by Fandom where you’ll find a slider allowing you to land on a score from zero to 100.
Fair to say, most entrants are probably going to opt for the ‘Favourable’ green region which features scores of 75 and above.
It’s one prediction per person, although you can edit your prediction right up until the contest closes on Tuesday November 17 at 11.59pm ET / Wednesday November 18 at 4.59am GMT.
All correct entries will, if you opt in, be entered into a sweepstakes draw where you could walk away with a $150, $250, or $500 Visa gift card.
Thousands of fans have already entered the draw and when you do enter, you’ll be able to see the median score based on the prediction of fellow fans.
Unfortunately, the contest is only available to residents of the United States and you have to be aged 18-plus to enter.
Winners are set to be drawn around November 25 and announced after November 30.
Many flocked to share their predictions in response to Metacritic sharing news of the contest.
“First 100/100 game in history of gaming. Mark my words,” replied one Twitter/X user.
“95 I’m gonna take a wild guess and say some will give it a lower score because of performance issues because of 30fps on consoles,” added another.
It appears that 98 is a very popular guess, making up the vast majority of responses to the tweet.

GTA VI ’s first ratings appear to have surfaced already after a number of scores were datamined from the PlayStation Store’s backend .
It’s claimed that GTA VI has 11 ratings with everyone so far awarding the title a perfect score of five out of five.
This has to be taken with a hefty pinch of salt though, as the supposedly datamined ratings haven’t been verified.
If they are real, they could belong to media and creators with the game in hand, or they could simply have been left by Rockstar Games developers. You do need a copy of a game in order to leave a review on the PlayStation Store.
It’s been a busy week for GTA VI, with the final countdown to launch well underway.
Rockstar Games announced GTA VI : The Festival , a once-in-a-lifetime launch party, and confirmed that the game will controversially run at 30fps , even on PS5 Pro.
Preloads are available now for those who have digitally pre-ordered the game, with those who opted for a code-in-a-box able to preload from tomorrow, on November 12.
GTA VI launches on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

articles.t: PlayStation 5 Crosses Major Sales Milestone Ahead of GTA 6 Launch
articles.chapeau: The PlayStation 5 has officially exceeded 100 million units sold worldwide in its lifetime.
articles.txt:
If ever there were a definitively good time to invest in a game console like the PlayStation 5 , it’d certainly be now, what with the looming release of Grand Theft Auto 6 in just a little over a week. I can’t speak to how many people have gone out and bought PS5s for the express purpose of playing that game, but considering it's the console's best-selling title , I have to imagine it’s more than a few, and coupling those with the players who have already invested in the PS5 since its initial release in 2020, the overall statistics are nothing to sneeze at.
According to newly-released sales statistics from Sony Interactive Entertainment , as of yesterday, November 10, 2026, the PlayStation 5 has officially surpassed 100 million units sold worldwide in its lifespan.
For six years out from launch, that’s pretty good, especially since it’s a stone’s throw from the approximately 102 million-unit record held by the original PlayStation console, though it is a very far cry from the over-160 million PlayStation 2s sold. Hey, it was literally one of the best-selling game consoles of all time, anyone would have trouble beating that.
According to Sony’s sales statistics, in Q1 and Q2 2026 combined, about 3.2 million PS5 units have been sold. For the record, the console’s all-time quarterly sales record was set in Q3 2024 at 9.5 million, and the all-time yearly record was set in 2023 at 20.8.
Incidentally, these sales statistics are based on “sell-in” units, which means the numbers sold to officially licensed resellers, i.e. regular stores you buy gaming hardware at. The statistics don’t cover the sell-through numbers, which is the number of consoles actually purchased from resellers by end users. Presumably, that number is smaller, but if retailers are ordering lots of PS5s, it means people are buying them in large quantities, so that still says a lot.
In Q1 and Q2 2026 combined, about 3.2 million PS5 units have been sold.
The statistics don’t yet have the sales numbers for consoles in Q3, which lasts from October to December, but I have a hunch that, with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 this month, those numbers are going to see at least some degree of lurch when they’re finally divulged. The stats sheet also doesn’t cover Q3’s software sales, but you can bet those are going to see a major hike for the same reason.
Despite how good all of these stats seem on paper, the reality of the situation is that the PS5’s overall sales for this year haven’t been especially hot. Comparing Q1 and Q2 statistics to years’ prior, both are smaller than every year from 2021 to 2025.
Granted, as I said, there is a nonzero chance we’re going to see a major lurch in the Q3 statistics; Q3, being the holiday season, usually sees a big jump every year, with sales doubling their usual rates from 2022 to 2025. With the once-in-a-generation winds of GTA 6 at its back, the PS5 could certainly recoup its failings in Q3 2026, though everyone who already has a PS5 or chooses to play that game elsewhere could hamper that projection.
Putting aside sales in 2020 and 2021, which were obviously hampered due to the COVID pandemic, it does seem like PS5 sales definitively peaked in 2023, and have been on a downswing since, with the primary suspected culprit being the console’s repeated price hikes and the gradual increase in cost of gaming as a hobby in the last couple of years.
Then again, it could just be that the PS5 is coming to the end of its time, and it’s time for the PS6 to take the reins, though in the current climate, it’s anyone’s guess how much that thing will end up costing.

articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI lands on Thursday, November 19, 2026, which leaves exactly eight days between today and the biggest scheduled launch in games this year. Rockstar Games confirmed the date in a short statement that read, in full, “Grand Theft Auto VI will now release on Thursday, November 19, 2026.” Coverage from Investor’s Business Daily, Bloomberg, MassLive and Yahoo Tech now frames the game as poised to steal the pop culture spotlight, and that framing is the story this analysis tests.
The distinction matters. A confirmed release date, a confirmed platform list and a confirmed price are facts. A pop culture takeover is a forecast. This piece separates the two, lays out what Rockstar and Microsoft have actually put on the record, and explains how publishers, console makers and retailers should read the next eight days. Readers following the commercial side can also see our earlier look at Take-Two’s pre-order comments and the missing totals .
Everything below sticks to documented details. Where the record stops, the article says so and labels the rest as analysis. That approach costs a few headline-friendly claims about sales records and audience size, but those claims are exactly what no official source has documented yet. For broader platform coverage, the gaming section tracks the launch window as it develops.

Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
The confirmed list is short, and every item on it comes from Rockstar Games or from Microsoft’s store listing. Rockstar is both developer and publisher. The release date is November 19, 2026. The game ships on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S. Xbox One owners can reach it through Xbox Cloud Gaming , which is a streaming route and not a native install.
Pricing is confirmed through the Microsoft Store. The standard edition of Grand Theft Auto VI costs $79.99. The Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. Those two numbers set the ceiling for what a typical buyer pays on day one, at least on Microsoft’s storefront.
Rockstar also explained why the date moved. In its words, the extra months will allow the studio to finish the game with the level of polish players have come to expect and deserve. That sentence is the only official reasoning on record for the schedule change, so any claim about a deeper cause, whether technical, financial or competitive, belongs in the speculation column.
The table below summarizes the confirmed record and the source type behind each line. It also serves as a reference for the rest of the article, because every later section builds on these entries and nothing else.
Investor’s Business Daily, Bloomberg, MassLive and Yahoo Tech have all run versions of the same story this week. The shared angle holds that Grand Theft Auto VI is about to move from a games-industry topic to a general-news and entertainment topic. Business desks care because the launch sits inside a holiday quarter. Lifestyle and local desks care because the series has a long record of turning up in conversation well beyond gaming circles.
That framing is a prediction, and the fact sheet for this story marks it as unconfirmed. No official source has documented an audience size, a sales figure, a record or a cultural-impact measurement for the game, because the game has not shipped. What exists is a pattern of attention. Pre-launch coverage is dense, the date is close, and the title is one of the few in games with name recognition among non-players.
Attention is not the same as impact. A launch can dominate headlines for a week and fade from conversation by the second Friday. Another can start quietly and become a shared reference point for months. Nobody can tell which path Grand Theft Auto VI will take until real players hold the real game. The honest reading of the current coverage is that expectation is high and the evidence for it is still circumstantial.
Three signals support the case for heavy attention. First, Rockstar’s fixed date gives every outlet a hard deadline to build coverage around. Second, a $79.99 price on a standard edition makes the game a news item on cost alone. Third, the platform list leaves out several major hardware families, which invites comparison stories. None of those signals proves a pop culture takeover, but together they explain why editors across business and entertainment desks assigned the story.

articles.t: GTA 6 : Même Hollywood commence à se préparer pour l'impact que va causer la sortie du jeu
articles.chapeau: Bon nombre de studios n’ont pas voulu se frotter à GTA 6 en cette fin d’année, à tort ou à raison. Le jeu de Rockstar va bel et bien [...]
articles.txt:
Bon nombre de studios n’ont pas voulu se frotter à GTA 6 en cette fin d’année, à tort ou à raison. Le jeu de Rockstar va bel et bien monopoliser l’espace médiatique (c’est déjà le cas), si bien qu’exister à ses côtés durant les prochaines semaines sera compliqué. et cela ne vaut pas que pour l’industrie du jeu vidéo. The Hollywood Reporter a fait le point sur l’impact que pourrait causer la sortie du jeu sur les films et séries à venir, et s’il n’est pas encore tout à fait palpable, une certaine crainte est présente.
GTA 6 n’occulte pas encore les sorties cinéma, mais tout le monde est tendu Pour mesurer les conséquences de la sortie de GTA 6 sur le cinéma et le monde de la télévision (plus précisément du streaming), le site est allé questionner Bart Spiegel, qui gère la division divertissement et sports chez PricewaterhouseCoopers (une grande entreprise d’audit et d’expertise comptable) :
« Il s’agira d’un tournant décisif, non seulement pour l’industrie du jeu vidéo, mais aussi pour tous les acteurs des secteurs des médias et du divertissement, qui devront faire face au fait qu’une partie de leur audience va délaisser leurs plateformes pour aller jouer à GTA 6 . »
Contrairement à l’industrie du jeu vidéo, celle du cinéma n’a pas pris de précautions particulières pour éviter GTA 6 puisque l’on note tout de même quelques sorties majeures, comme le prochain Hunger Games qui a réalisé de bonnes préventes. Malgré tout, un cadre d’une grande chaîne de cinéma reconnait que quiconque dans l’industrie qui joue un peu sait à quel point GTA 6 aura un impact , sans savoir dans quelle mesure.
Le week-end de lancement sera peut-être difficile, mais Geoff Keighley (producteur des Game Awards) a lui aussi son avis sur la question et pense que cela va s’étendre sur plusieurs semaines. Jusqu’à la sortie de Dune 3 et Avengers: Doomsday ? C’est bien possible, même si ces films sont forcément un peu à part du reste de l’industrie pour les personnes interrogées.
C’est surtout le milieu du streaming qui risque d’être impacté , comme le confie un représentant qui travaille sur une série qui sera bientôt diffusée (sans que l’on sache laquelle) :
Même l’industrie de la musique se prépare à un séisme , avec l’album du jeu qui devrait truster largement le haut des classements des plateformes de streaming. Le plus difficile sera surtout d’exister sur les réseaux sociaux. Cela pourrait impacter le marketing de ces films et de ces séries, étant donné que le jeu va occuper une grande place dans les discussions. Réponse dans quelques jours.

articles.chapeau: Neuf jours avant la sortie, Rockstar Games publie une bande-annonce mettant en avant le préchargement de Grand Theft Auto VI sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S.
articles.txt:
Neuf jours avant la sortie officielle de Grand Theft Auto VI , Rockstar Games a surpris la communauté en publiant un nouveau court trailer. Cette vidéo accompagne le lancement du préchargement, opération qui a débuté aujourd’hui sur les consoles PlayStation 5 et Microsoft Xbox Series X|S. Ce téléchargement anticipé avait déjà permis, dès le matin, de révéler plusieurs détails inédits sur le jeu. L’événement est également marqué par un festival musical dédié ainsi que de nombreuses actions marketing à Miami, ville réelle qui sert de modèle à la fiction de Leonida et Vice City.
Dans le cadre de ces festivités, des stands de vente portant les noms de Burger Shot et Cluckin’ Bell sont installés au Kaseya Center. La veille de la sortie, l’équipe des Miami Heat affronte les Milwaukee Bucks sur un terrain aménagé dans le style de Vice City. Le clip disponible sur la page officielle du jeu et sur YouTube présente des personnages secondaires inconnus jusqu’à présent, des extraits de missions et des aperçus de l’immense monde ouvert.
Contrairement aux vidéos précédentes, les deux protagonistes principaux, Jason et Lucia, ne sont pas au centre de l’attention dans ce nouveau spot. L’action se concentre plutôt sur des poursuites à travers Vice City, diverses interventions policières incluant potentiellement une perquisition d’appartement, et de nombreuses scènes de vie nocturne dans des clubs lors de fêtes animées. Ce changement de focus offre un regard différent sur l’univers du jeu, mettant en avant l’ambiance et les détails de l’environnement plutôt que les seuls héros.
Concernant les spécifications techniques, le préchargement nécessite jusqu’à 212 Go d’espace libre selon la console utilisée. Sur PlayStation, le téléchargement a commencé à minuit, tandis que sur Xbox, il a débuté une heure plus tard, à 1h00. Le jeu ne sera toutefois jouable qu’à la date de sortie officielle, fixée au 19 novembre. Initialement, le téléchargement anticipé était prévu pour le 12 novembre, mais Rockstar avait avancé ce délai de deux jours pour les précommandes digitales début novembre.
Dès quelques heures après le début du préchargement, des dataminers ont analysé les métadonnées accessibles. Ces données contiennent des indices pointant vers une version plus récente de PSSR sur la PS5 Pro ainsi qu’un mode 120 Hz. Par ailleurs, aucune version pour PC n’a encore été officiellement annoncée, bien qu’elle pourrait apparaître dès le premier trimestre de l’année prochaine. Sur le plan commercial, le jeu est actuellement disponible à partir de 79,28 euros sur la PlayStation 5.

articles.txt:
Après des mois de rumeurs, aussi bien positives que négatives, Rockstar a tranché ce mardi 10 novembre, dans un billet publié à l’ouverture du préchargement du jeu : GTA 6 tournera bien à 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles , y compris la très puissante PS5 Pro .
Depuis cette annonce, la déception est massive chez les joueurs qui restaient optimistes sur un meilleur framerate pour la console la plus chère du marché, vendue 899,99 euros depuis la hausse de prix d’avril. Certains estiment que leur achat n’a finalement servi à rien, qu’un meilleur ray tracing et une meilleure qualité d’image ne peuvent pas compenser une fréquence d’images identique à la PS5 de base . D’autres estiment qu’il est même indéfendable en 2026 de proposer un jeu avec un tel plafond de performance.
Rockstar n’en est pas à son coup d’essai. La plupart de ses jeux sont sortis plafonnés à 30 FPS sur console, et certains n’ont reçu un mode 60 FPS que des années plus tard, sur les machines suivantes. GTA V tourne ainsi en 1440p à 60 FPS sur PS5 Pro. Actuellement, Red Dead Redemption 2 est lui encore bloqué à 30 FPS sur PS5, 8 ans après sa sortie.
On s’en doutait pourtant ces derniers mois avec les différents trailers du jeu et notamment l’Aperçu étendu, analysé de toutes parts, y compris par Frandroid . Derrière cette limitation, les joueurs pointent du doigt les choix techniques de Sony, à commencer par le processeur de la console.

Dans notre dossier dédié au rôle du processeur pour le gaming , nous précisions notamment que c’est le processeur qui, sur les ordres du moteur du jeu, envoie les fameux draw calls à la carte graphique via une API dédiée. On parle ici de la géométrie, des meshs d’une scène, que le GPU dessine ensuite avec un shader spécifique (texture, lumière, couleur).
Surtout, le processeur gère la logique du jeu et tous ses systèmes, comme la météo, les PNJ, la circulation, la physique, la balistique de certains objets et même la gravité.
Un jeu comme GTA 6 fait tourner un très grand nombre de systèmes, dont beaucoup fonctionnent de concert en plein gameplay. Au-delà du rendu graphique, ils pèsent lourd sur le processeur. Or, la PS5 Pro est pour ainsi dire en retard à ce niveau.
On le savait dès les premières fuites sur la PS5 Pro : Sony a nettement privilégié la partie graphique au détriment du processeur. articles.t: GTA 6 : un DLC officiel gratuit révélé par une fuite pour le plus grand plaisir des joueurs
articles.chapeau: À quelques semaines de la sortie de GTA 6, une fuite Discord évoque une campagne Hexagon avec GTA 6 DLC gratuit et récompense mystère. Contenu, dates, enjeux : ce bonus soulève déjà bien des questions.
articles.txt:
À quelques semaines de la sortie de GTA 6, une fuite Discord évoque une campagne Hexagon avec GTA 6 DLC gratuit et récompense mystère. Contenu, dates, enjeux : ce bonus soulève déjà bien des questions.
GTA 6 n’est même pas encore sorti et un premier « DLC » gratuit fait déjà parler de lui. Une fuite du code de Discord mentionne une campagne marketing baptisée « Hexagon » , centrée sur Grand Theft Auto VI , avec thème dédié et récompense mystérieuse à la clé.
Derrière ce nom de code se cacherait ce que certains médias décrivent déjà comme un premier GTA 6 DLC gratuit . Entre contenu cosmétique, éventuelle récompense in‑game et bonus de pré‑lancement, la communauté s’interroge sur ce que cette collaboration pourrait réellement offrir.
Le dataminer Wumpus Central a fouillé une version de test de Discord et repéré une campagne GTA 6 Discord nommée « Hexagon ». Dans les fichiers figurent une icône d’application GTA 6 , un app theme aux couleurs de Vice City et une police de pseudo inspirée de la typo officielle du jeu. Des sites comme RockstarINTEL ou GTA BOOM ont rapidement relayé l’information.
Plus intéressant pour les joueurs, le code mentionne une « quest with unknown reward » qui « may be coming soon during the campaign too », selon Wumpus Central sur X. GamingBible parle déjà de « first free in‑game reward » pour GTA 6 , d’où l’expression de contenu additionnel GTA 6 ou de « DLC gratuit ». Mais rien ne prouve encore que la récompense sera utilisable dans le jeu plutôt que limitée à Discord.
Les Discord Quest sont des campagnes où l’utilisateur doit accomplir une action pour décrocher une récompense : jouer à un jeu un certain temps, regarder un trailer ou participer à un événement. En 2022, par exemple, des quêtes liées à Fortnite Paradise permettaient de débloquer des objets in‑game, tandis que d’autres campagnes n’offraient que des cosmétiques Discord comme des décorations d’avatar.
Pour cette quête Discord GTA 6 , plusieurs scénarios sont plausibles : simple bonus Discord (thème exclusif, décorations de profil), skin d’arme ou tenue unique dans GTA 6 , voire petit avantage de pré‑commande lié au compte Rockstar Social Club. Dans tous les cas, il faudra très probablement accepter la Quest dans l’interface officielle, puis remplir l’objectif indiqué. Attention aux faux liens « GTA 6 Discord Hexagon » envoyés en message privé, terrain idéal pour le phishing .
D’après le datamine relayé par RockstarINTEL , la campagne Hexagon débuterait le 17 novembre 2026 à 18 h 00 UTC, soit 19 h en France, deux jours avant la sortie officielle de GTA 6 le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S . Les utilisateurs gratuits pourraient participer jusqu’au 8 décembre 2026, tandis que les abonnés Discord Nitro auraient jusqu’au 15 février 2027.
Ce possible bonus GTA 6 avant la sortie s’inscrirait dans une stratégie où Rockstar Games mise sur des collaborations et des freebies plutôt que sur des DLC solo payants dès le lancement. Officiellement, ni Rockstar ni Discord n’ont confirmé la campagne Hexagon, qui pourrait encore être modifiée ou annulée. Les joueurs en quête de GTA 6 DLC gratuit ont donc tout intérêt à surveiller les annonces officielles et l’onglet Quest de Discord à l’approche du 17 novembre.

articles.t: GTA 6 First Review Scores Appear Online Early
articles.chapeau: GTA VI is finally almost here, and it seems as though some impressions of the game have surfaced online early.
articles.txt:
By James Lynch Published Nov 11, 2026, 5:38 AM EST James is a gaming writer from London who has spent thousands of hours exploring titles from every genre. Though he has a particular affinity for multiplayer titles like World of Warcraft, Destiny 2 and League of Legends, he has also put thousands of hours into single-player experiences, from deep RPGs to epic PC strategies. When he's not playing or writing, he can usually be found supporting his beloved Brentford FC. Sign in to your ScreenRant account The wait for Grand Theft Auto VI has been a genuinely monumental one, with all the delays and speculation only making the time we've been standing by to play it feel even longer. That said, the game is finally almost here, and we're a little over a week out from the November 19 release date at the time of writing.
While we're all assuming that the years of effort that Rockstar have put into developing the game will pay dividends, and we're all going to be playing the standout game of recent times, we don't actually know that just yet. Until we get to try it for ourselves and work through the story and multiplayer modes (eventually), we can't really give the developer their flowers.
We shouldn't have long to wait until the embargo passes, and we can find out officially from those who have played it what their thoughts are, but before then, reviews have started to appear online and they are just as positive as you might expect.
Jason rides a motorcycle as he runs away from police in GTA 6. Over on Reddit , one user shared a post with a screenshot from the PlayStation store of GTA VI's official page. On it, there are now 11 reviews for the game in total, all of which are currently five stars. The interesting part of that is that the store on the platform usually requires players to have purchased and played a game in order to review it.
That leaves very few options for how this happened, with one being that those who were given early access have broken cover and added their feedback to the store's ecosystem. At the moment, these appear to just be ratings for the game, rather than written feedback of any time, but it could be a sign that the game is set to deliver on the scale that many are expecting.
Many weighed in with their own guesses at how good the finished game would be, with one saying , "Quite a bit of hate both valid and bs around the game, so a game on this scale will probably fluctuate a fair amount, unless I am underestimating the hype compared to the hate/idc for GTA but will rate it poorly crowd."
While another added that a perfect score may be impossible, saying , "Even if the game is good enough to warrant a 99, it may be impossible. OOT came out when much fewer journalists were about (it only has 22 reviews, RDR2 has 99), and all it takes is a couple giving a good-but-not-incredible score and you haven't got a 99."
In the end, the proverbial proof in the pudding will come when you have played Grand Theft Auto VI for yourself, and though reviews can act as an excellent guide to what to expect, a game as big as this one is going to generate all sorts of opinions. With just eight days to go until it releases to the masses, let's hope we're not in the timeline where it fails to hit the expectations of the audience.

Rockstar Games says the free printable Grand Theft Auto VI cover-art poster and Leonida map go live on November 19, 2026, and a double-sided physical version will sell for $0.99 through the Rockstar Store, according to Vice . That announcement is the only part of this story with an official stamp on it. Everything about the GTA 6 physical pre-order poster showing up in boxed copies instead of a map rests on a retail leak that nobody has tied to a named store.
The leak, as reported, says some physical GTA 6 pre-orders may come with a poster where fans expected a folded map. No retailer, product SKU, pre-order price, release date or bonus list has been established by that report. Rockstar has not said that any poster or map ships inside retail packaging. So the headline is a live rumor with a confirmed backdrop, and this analysis keeps those two layers apart.
The timing matters because the game is close. Launch day is November 19, management reaffirmed that date on November 9–11, 2026 and said development was complete, and our earlier look at the rating still pending with eight content descriptors showed how many small details remain open this late. A poster-or-map question looks minor next to a 212 GB download, but collectors, retailers and Rockstar’s own store all have money riding on the answer.

The physical version follows later. Rockstar describes the timing as “shortly after launch,” a phrase Vice quotes directly, and no exact date has been announced.
Pricing is simple. The physical item costs $0.99 by itself, or it comes free with any purchase from the Rockstar Store. Press Start Australia headlined the same announcement as a map and poster that is free digitally at launch or sold for $1. Rounding aside, the outlets agree on the structure: free file, cheap paper copy, store-only sales channel.

articles.t: GTA 6 pourrait finalement proposer un mode 40 FPS sur PS5 Pro grâce au 120 Hz et à un PSSR amélioré
articles.chapeau: À quelques jours du lancement de GTA 6, une datamine du préchargement PS5 Pro révèle un mode 120 Hz et un PSSR 13.60 inédit. Faut-il y voir le signe d’un futur mode 40 FPS très convoité ?
articles.txt:
À quelques jours du lancement de GTA 6, une datamine du préchargement PS5 Pro révèle un mode 120 Hz et un PSSR 13.60 inédit. Faut-il y voir le signe d’un futur mode 40 FPS très convoité ?
À quelques jours de la sortie console de Grand Theft Auto VI , fixée au 19 novembre 2026, un détail enfoui dans le préchargement PS5 agite la communauté. En fouillant ces fichiers mis en ligne dès le 10 novembre, le dataminer Tex2 , figure de GTAForums , a repéré un mode 120 Hz dédié à la PS5 Pro et une nouvelle version de la technologie d’upscaling PSSR de Sony .
Relayée par RockstarINTEL et la presse spécialisée, la fuite mentionne un module « MFSR / PSSR 13.60 » ainsi qu’une absence totale de tag VRR . Ce combo 120 Hz sans VRR correspond parfaitement à un mode 40 FPS , même si, officiellement, Rockstar ne promet toujours que 30 FPS sur consoles, avec un rendu interne probablement autour de 1440p upscalé en 4K. De quoi espérer une GTA 6 plus fluide sur PS5 Pro, sans aucune garantie pour l’instant.
Une datamine ne pirate pas le jeu, elle lit simplement les capacités que le moteur déclare à la console. Dans le build PS5 Pro de GTA 6 , Tex2 a repéré un flag « High Frame Rate 120 Hz » et un « High CPU Frequency Mode », ce qui confirme un profil distinct de la PS5. On y voit aussi un bloc PSSR en version 13.60, alors que de nombreux titres « PS5 Pro Enhanced » restent sur la branche 13.00A, et la build PS5 standard ne mentionne pas QSSR , l’upscaler des consoles non Pro.
Sur un téléviseur 120 Hz, un mode 40 FPS s’intègre bien, car 120 divisé par 40 donne trois rafraîchissements par image, avec un temps d’affichage moindre qu’à 30 FPS. Associé au PSSR 13.60, conçu pour approcher la 4K tout en calculant moins de pixels en interne, ce profil donne à la PS5 Pro un terrain pour viser un framerate plus élevé. Mais, comme l’a rappelé Rob Nelson , co-directeur de Rockstar North , cité par Notebookcheck, les développeurs « visent les 30 fps pour la date de sortie du 19 novembre », un monde ouvert comme Leonida restant très gourmand en processeur.
Passer de 30 à 40 FPS représenterait environ 33 % d’images en plus, une latence un peu plus faible et des mouvements plus naturels, à condition de disposer d’une TV 120 Hz HDMI 2.1 et d’activer le 120 Hz dans les réglages système de la console. Mais les métadonnées ne prouvent que ce que le moteur peut faire, pas ce que Rockstar Games exposera dans les options, et avec une PS5 Pro vendue autour de 899,99 € en France, beaucoup attendront la présentation officielle des modes graphiques et les premiers tests avant de décider si un 40 FPS justifie l’investissement.

articles.t: Bethesda denies The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel leak of news on Skyrim anniversary

articles.txt:
Todd Howard finally announced the full name of the most anticipated Bethesda game. The studio head also cautioned fans not to expect more news soon, casting doubt on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel release date . Still, rumors emerged teasing that the Skyrim 15th Anniversary could bring a surprise. Sadly, the publisher has now dismissed the possibility with a Reddit post .

Reece “Kiwi Talkz” Reilly then made a vaguer statement about a November 11th development. Even so, it was not necessarily related to the open-world RPG .
Waiting since 2011 for a sequel, desperate fans look for any reason to be optimistic. Xbox would also like to see progress with its popular franchises to boost sinking profits. The reality is that an Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel release date in 2027 or even 2028 has become unlikely.
Bloomberg insider Jason Schreier recently warned the Bethesda game wouldn’t surface for more than two years. He said he learned of a development timetable making 2029 a realistic target. Windows Central’s Jez Corden echoed that thinking in his own report.

articles.t: GTA 6 could get FSR 4.1 support on Xbox Series X|S to compete with PSSR on PS5 Pro
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 has been confirmed to get support for PSSR on the PS5 Pro, though the exact version is unclear. A new report has suggested that the game could come with some upscaling technology on the Xbox Series consoles as well.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 pre-loads have started, and sure enough, people are digging into the downloadable files. A recent PS5 datamine revealed the presence of PSSR, or PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, in GTA 6 , and now a deep dive into the Xbox Series X/S files has revealed the presence of FSR, or FidelityFX Super Resolution.
PSSR is Sony’s AI-driven upscaling technology specifically designed for the PS5 Pro. The base PS5 also has a version of it called QSSR, or Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Following the datamine, Rockstar officially confirmed that PSSR will be available in GTA 6 , though the datamine suggested it would support a newer or different version of the upscaling technology.
Xbox, on the other hand, was recently added to the list of devices that will be getting FSR 4.1 support. While AMD did not confirm when that would be, some developers already have access to it, including older versions of the technology. It won’t be surprising if Rockstar is one of those developers, with early access to FSR 4.1, which increases the possibility of GTA 6 getting FSR 4.1 support sooner rather than later. That said, chances of the game getting FSR 4.1 at launch are slim, but at least it will come with some version of the upscaling tech at launch, as indicated by the Xbox Series package datamine.
It also makes sense that at some point in the future, GTA 6 would be updated to the latest version of FSR for Xbox Series console owners. As to how this would affect the game’s performance on Xbox consoles, remains to be seen.

articles.t: GTA 6 PS5 reviews already live on PlayStation Store before embargo and release date
articles.chapeau: Anxious players have managed to post GTA 6 review scores on the PlayStation Store. In some cases, PSN accounts can share ratings prior to release dates. Likely suspects are media members testing the PS5 game ahead of the November 18th embargo.
articles.txt:
The GTA 6 review embargo reportedly doesn’t end until November 18th, the day before the release date . Regardless, ratings are already appearing on the PlayStation Store. PS Store DB , which monitors the marketplace’s backend, discovered 11 entries producing a 5/5 score.
Dataminer Cokymoky later reported there are actually 12 ratings, averaging 4.67/5.0. 92 percent of users gave the PS5 game 5 stars, while one person believed it deserves a single star (now changed to 5/5). Sony started testing written reviews in August 2024, but Cokymoky69 hasn’t found any text on the PlayStation Store.
PSN accounts can judge a digital purchase without waiting for official launches. There are also no minimum playtime requirements. One explanation is that the mystery players are sites or YouTube channels that Rockstar sent codes to. While preloads have begun for buyers, actually booting the title may have unlocked their ability to register scores.
Microsoft is even more lax about its marketplace policies. Months ahead of the GTA 6 release date, ratings flooded the Xbox Store. Although it’s a questionable practice, anyone who pre-orders a game can share their opinion early. The Rockstar project currently boasts a perfect 5/5 after nearly 10,000 submissions.
The small sample of GTA 6 PS5 reviews on the PlayStation Store backend may not reflect the post-launch consensus. Nevertheless, if the activity is from journalists, they could preview Metacritic ratings .
Given the record-setting sales , fans have questioned whether the views of the media will matter. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pushed back on that thinking in a May interview, saying critical reception remains important . He praised the quality of Rockstar’s work, noting past titles scored in the mid-to-high 90s.
Most PSN users with pre-orders must hold off until the GTA 6 release date for reviews. As with Xbox and PS5 preloads, New Zealand players will be the first to explore Leonida .

Rockstar reveals GTA 6 console performance targets and PS5 Pro upgrades
articles.chapeau: Rockstar Games has confirmed that GTA 6 will target 30 FPS across the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles, including the PS5 Pro. Sony's upgraded console will instead receive exclusive ray-traced shadows and PSSR upscaling, while a 60 FPS performance mode remains unconfirmed.
articles.txt:
With Grand Theft Auto VI preloads now underway, Rockstar Games has finally shed more light on how its highly anticipated open-world title will perform on current-generation consoles. As many had suspected, the game will target 30 FPS across the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S lineup, including Sony's more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro.
According to Rockstar's official announcement , the 30 FPS target was chosen to maintain the density and visual fidelity of Leonida's expansive open world. This effectively puts an end to speculation about the PS5 Pro delivering a substantially higher frame rate at launch, although Rockstar has not explicitly ruled out additional graphics modes.
Instead, the PS5 Pro will distinguish itself through improved image quality. Rockstar has confirmed support for PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), Sony's AI-powered upscaling technology, alongside ray-traced shadows exclusive to the upgraded console.
Interestingly, recent datamining findings suggest that GTA VI could use a newer implementation of PSSR than existing PS5 Pro titles. References to version 13.60 were discovered in the preload metadata, compared with version 13.00A reportedly used by games such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Assassin's Creed Shadows .
Another interesting discovery is a reference to 120 Hz output . This has fueled speculation about a possible 40 FPS mode in GTA 6 , which would provide a middle ground between 30 FPS and 60 FPS on compatible displays. A 40 FPS presentation can fit evenly into a 120 Hz refresh cycle, making it a viable alternative for graphically demanding games. However, the presence of a 120 Hz option does not confirm that Rockstar intends to offer it.
The preload metadata also reportedly lacks references to QSSR , Sony's newer upscaling solution for the standard PS5. That does not conclusively rule out its inclusion in the final game, but it suggests that the base console may not receive the same upscaling improvements as its Pro counterpart.
Beyond graphical enhancements, Rockstar has confirmed that the PlayStation 5 version will support DualSense haptic feedback, improved spatial audio through Tempest 3D Audio and optimised loading times. The developer has not detailed equivalent platform-specific enhancements for the Xbox Series X or Series S. Not that there are too many to begin with, except Quick Resume, maybe.
It is worth noting that the 30 FPS target does not necessarily guarantee a locked frame rate under all circumstances. Similarly, Rockstar has not disclosed the rendering resolutions or graphical compromises required for the Xbox Series S, which has considerably less GPU power and available memory than the Series X.
GTA 6 launches on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloads are already available, with Rockstar confirming that players will need up to 212 GB of available storage, depending on their console.

articles.txt:
Copied Is GTA 6 Online release on the cards? It certainly will launch, but the conversation is on about when - soon, or sometime in the nebulous future. GTA Online has been one of gaming’s biggest cash cows for over a decade, so it was never going to be simple when it came to GTA 6 Online's plans. This game is all about the multiplayer mode and most gamers consider it to be as good as, if not better, than the single-player mode. While rumours have suggested the online mode might not arrive until sometime in 2027, a fresh discovery from data miners is complicating that timeline.
Buried inside the GTA 6 release date build are strings suggesting multiplayer groundwork already exists, even if it won’t be switched on come launch day.
The findings come from PlayStation Game Size , who dug through the GTA 6 release build and spotted references including “joinSession,” “launchActivity,” and “launchMultiplayerActivity.” These strings point toward functionality for creating or joining sessions, exactly the kind of backend groundwork multiplayer features typically need.
That said, none of this confirms online mode is landing on November 19th, it simply suggests Rockstar may have built the framework in advance so a future rollout can slot in smoothly rather than arrive as a bolt-on later.
History offers some hope for an early-ish arrival too. GTA Online famously launched just two weeks after GTA 5’s solo campaign, while Red Dead Redemption 2’s multiplayer beta surfaced roughly a month post-release. Still, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier has downplayed expectations of an imminent announcement, suggesting fans may be waiting until 2027 for co-op missions to materialise. Why the wait? Well, Rockstar took some 13 years to roll out GTA 6. GTA 6 Online getting delayed is par for the course.
GTA Online remains an enormous earner for Rockstar even today, and that profitability alone gives the studio little incentive to rush players away from it.
Twitch CEO Dan Clancy has echoed similar sentiment, noting that a 2027 GTA 6 Online launch would likely generate a much bigger viewership spike than an earlier rollout squeezed in alongside the base game’s launch hype.
Adding to the intrigue, Discord logs from a past Rockstar employee tribunal referenced a 32-participant multiplayer test session dating back to October 2025, suggesting internal testing has been underway for a while now.
With GTA 6 pre-loads beginning November 10th in New Zealand before spreading worldwide, data miners are expected to keep digging, and more clues about GTA 6 Online release date may not be far behind.

articles.t: GTA 6 Xbox leak hints at display and audio features PlayStation users won't get as preload goes live
articles.chapeau: While PlayStation has been touted as the best way to play GTA 6, a physical copy leak hints at Xbox having an advantage with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos.
articles.txt:
The big day is finally here, and we're in the end zone for the next Grand Theft Auto. It's been 13 years since GTA V raced into our lives and changed the world of video games forever.
Becoming the most profitable entertainment product of all time, GTA V 's success has been propped up by GTA Online and the fact that it still makes over $1 million a day.
The bar is in the stratosphere when it comes to GTA VI , but with it supposedly making $751 million in preorders alone, and tipped to make $5 billion in its first week alone, something tells us Rockstar Games will be just fine.
GTA VI has inadvertently reignited the gaming wars, with a fierce debate over whether PlayStation or Xbox is the ultimate way to play. Now, a physical copy leak has potentially crowned Xbox as the winner.
There's been a lot of chatter about the PlayStation 5 Pro being the definitive way to play GTA VI , with the upcoming automotive adventure even boasting a 'PS5 Pro Enhanced' label on the PS Store. Sony has done a massive marketing push to promote its souped-up credentials, and we've seen accusations of scalping as PS5 Pro console prices have soared well beyond their $900 MSRP.
We already covered how your base console can get something of a PS5 Pro-inspired boost thanks to a few simple changes, while the addition of FSR 4.1 could give the Xbox Series family its own mid-generation refresh, but that's only if Rockstar decides to add it to GTA VI .
Continuing the good news for the green team, a GTA VI box leak seemingly reveals that the game will support Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos on Xbox. Whereas the PlayStation 5 version relies on standard HDR10, Dolby Vision produces more accurate colors.
Basically, premium TVs that support Dolby Vision can use frame-by-frame dynamic metadata to automatically balance peak brightness and make those vibrant neon signs of Vice City really pop.
Elsewhere, PlayStation relies on its Tempest 3D Audio engine that can pass a Dolby Atmos signal over HDMI to an external soundbar, meaning it's converted instead of being a native part, and there can be some spatial translation gaps.
Xbox treats Dolby Atmos as a native system-wide audio engine that maps objects into a 3D space, optimizing it for home cinema setups.
Chances are that you already have your console of choice by now, and with just nine days to go (at the time of writing), you can officially preload GTA VI ahead of November 19. Both PlayStation and Xbox will require 212 GB of storage, so you'd better start clearing out those games you haven't played in a while.
GTA VI preloads were originally penciled in for November 12, but giving us a bit of extra time to prepare ourselves, they're going live on November 10.
This means anyone who has pre-ordered a digital copy of the game will be able to download it and jump straight back into Vice City when GTA VI goes live on November 19.
Whereas PlayStation owners have a staggered regional rollout from 12:00 AM local time on 10 November, Xbox went with a global simultaneous launch from 12:00 AM GMT.
For physical copy owners, copies are supposed to start shipping or arriving from November 12, meaning you can preload via the code inside your box.
There's plenty of time to get yourselves ready for the GTA VI launch, but make sure you don't miss the boat on what could be the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

articles.t: Une fuite du boîtier physique de GTA 6 sur Xbox révèle de possibles avantages par rapport à la version PS5

articles.txt:
Sony a présenté les consoles PS5 comme le meilleur moyen de jouer au nouveau titre de Rockstar . Certains propriétaires de consoles Microsoft se sont sentis délaissés au fil du déroulement de la campagne marketing . Pourtant, une fuite du boîtier physique confirme que la version Xbox de GTA 6 bénéficie d'avantages visuels et sonores exclusifs.
À l'approche de la date de sortie de GTA 6 , fixée au 19 novembre, des images du boîtier PS5 ont déjà circulé sur les réseaux sociaux. Au lieu d'une carte, Rockstar y a inclus un poster recto verso. Désormais, videotech a partagé le dos du boîtier Xbox, qui révèle des détails sur les formats vidéo et audio compatibles.
Les fidèles des Series X et S devraient pouvoir profiter du Dolby Vision et du Dolby Atmos en option. Le Dolby Vision peut présenter des avantages par rapport au HDR grâce à des métadonnées dynamiques optimisées pour des scènes spécifiques. Il en résulte des couleurs et des niveaux de luminosité plus précis dans les jeux et les films.
Au grand dam des passionnés de home cinéma, les consoles Xbox proposent le Dolby Vision, contrairement à leur rivale, la PS5. Les fans de PlayStation s’appuient sur le HDR10 , qui reste très performant. Quoi qu’il en soit, les marques de téléviseurs OLED comme Sony et LG mettent en avant le Dolby Vision comme argument de vente.
Bien que l’attention se soit surtout portée sur les graphismes, les projets cinématographiques de Rockstar offrent également un son immersif. Le boîtier physique de GTA 6 sur Xbox indique que l’audio spatial Dolby Atmos sera disponible sur les consoles de Microsoft. Les jeux utilisant cette technologie produisent des effets sonores positionnels précis qui reflètent l’action à l’écran.
À la demande des joueurs, la PS5 a ajouté la prise en charge du Dolby Atmos lors d’une mise à jour en septembre 2023. Malgré cela, les jeux sont d’abord calibrés pour l’audio Tempest 3D de Sony , avant que le son ne soit converti en Atmos. Le résultat final varie et peut être tout aussi impressionnant, voire supérieur. Néanmoins, de nombreux auditeurs préfèrent l’autre solution dans les installations surround dotées d’enceintes en hauteur.
Les révélations sur la version Xbox de GTA 6 ne devraient pas modifier l’ important écart de ventes en précommande rapporté. Les fuites liées au préchargement laissent entendre que la PS5 Pro offrira une fréquence d’images ou un taux de rafraîchissement plus élevé. Pour le reste, les analystes s’attendent à des performances comparables sur la Series X et la console PS5 de base .

articles.t: GTA 6 Preorders Beat Forecasts as NBA 2K27 Falls Short
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 preorders are tracking far above Take-Two's plan before the Nov 19 launch, while NBA 2K27 missed its forecast. What the Q2 numbers mean for you.
articles.txt:
Take-Two says GTA 6 preorders far exceed its plan 10 days before the Nov 19 launch, but net bookings fell 18% to $1.6B as NBA 2K27 missed. Here's why.
Take-Two Interactive says GTA 6 preorders are "tracking far in excess of our initial expectations," ten days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19, 2026. The publisher shared the update with its fiscal second quarter results on November 9, but it did not give a single preorder number.
The same report shows the other side of a GTA year. NBA 2K27 sold more than 4 million copies and still missed Take-Two's forecast, and CEO Strauss Zelnick believes GTA 6 itself is part of the reason.
Strong enough for Take-Two to use very big words. In the official earnings release , Zelnick said, "The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is ten days away and, with pre-orders continuing to reach unprecedented levels, we expect to deliver an historic year for our company."
On the earnings call he added that "the numbers will speak for themselves soon enough." That is a polite way of saying the real figures come after launch. GTA VI arrives on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Take-Two's lineup table still lists no PC version. If you have not set up your console yet, our GTA 6 preload guide covers start times and the 212GB download.
NBA 2K27 came out on September 4 and posted the second best net bookings in the series' history. Net bookings is Take-Two's main sales measure: everything it sold digitally or shipped to stores in the period. Even so, the game landed below the company's own target.
Zelnick told IGN, in comments reported by Kotaku , "It has been a crowded period, and we do think that GTA 6 coming has had an influence on the consumer." In other words, some players may be saving their money for Vice City. He was relaxed about it with Bloomberg: "If your lunch is going to be eaten, I'd rather be the one eating it." President Karl Slatoff was more careful on the call, saying "it's really hard to know exactly" why the game fell short.
The quarter ended on September 30, so it contains no GTA VI sales at all. Recurrent consumer spending, meaning money players spend inside games they already own (virtual currency, add-ons and in-game purchases), fell 9%. Take-Two had guided for a 5% drop.
Net bookings also missed Take-Two's own range of $1.62 billion to $1.67 billion, and Bloomberg says Wall Street expected about $1.65 billion. The full year outlook of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion stayed the same, and the October to December quarter alone is guided at $3.35 billion to $3.50 billion. GamesIndustry.biz notes that operating costs should rise about 21% in that quarter, mostly because of GTA 6 marketing.
Mostly, it suggests November 19 is holding. Take-Two repeated its $8 billion forecast and its launch date ten days out, with no hint of another delay. Rockstar's older game is still a giant too: GTA V has sold nearly 235 million copies, and the GTA+ membership grew by double digits last quarter.
Expect heavy server traffic and a crowded launch week, much like the pressure Sony pointed to when it discussed falling PS5 sales ahead of GTA 6 . PS5 Pro owners also have something to look forward to, since a datamine points to a 120Hz mode for GTA 6 .
A publisher calling its own preorders "unprecedented" is not proof, so the real test is the first sales figure after launch. Still, the NBA 2K27 miss tells us something useful: GTA 6 is pulling money out of gamers' wallets before it even ships. For Take-Two, a weak quarter is the price of one of the biggest game launches ever, and it looks happy to pay it.

Coverage from Cinelinx and Nintendo Life has framed the run-up as the build toward the biggest release in entertainment history, a label the publisher itself has not claimed.
That gap between headline and record book is the real story today. The confirmed facts are strong on their own: a $79.99 standard edition, pre-orders that opened at midnight local time on June 25, 2026, and a physical edition that ships as a download code with no disc. Our earlier look at the install-size claims circulating before preload showed how quickly unverified numbers spread when a release gets this big.
This analysis separates what Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar have actually confirmed from what the market is projecting. It covers the timeline, the price, the packaging, the money at stake for Sony and Microsoft, and four predictions for launch week. Anything the official sources do not state stays marked as unconfirmed.

Start with the short list of facts that hold up under scrutiny. Grand Theft Auto VI is developed and published by Rockstar Games, a label owned by Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. The release date is November 19, 2026. The launch platforms are PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The standard edition costs $79.99.
Pre-orders began June 25, 2026, at midnight local time, which means players in each region saw the store pages open as their own clock rolled over. Pre-loading starts November 10, 2026, so anyone who ordered digitally can have the files on their console before launch day. Standard physical versions contain a download code and do not include a disc, per the official release information.
Take-Two describes the game as featuring “a single-player experience set in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet.” That sentence is the closest the publisher comes to a superlative. It describes the game relative to earlier entries in the series. It makes no claim about the wider entertainment industry, and that distinction matters when headlines start to stretch it.
The table below sorts the public record into what is confirmed and what is not. Treat the second column as a watch list rather than a set of facts.
The GTA 6 release date has been stable in the official materials, and that consistency counts for something. Players have had months to plan around November 19. The only dated checkpoint left before launch is the preload window opening on November 10, and the three confirmed dates run in order: pre-orders on June 25, preload on November 10, launch on November 19.
Pre-loading is more than a convenience. When a download of this scale opens, network providers, console storefronts and publishers all see a demand spike days before the game even unlocks. A staggered preload spreads that load across the nine days before launch instead of concentrating it on the morning of November 19. Players who wait until launch day to start downloading take on avoidable risk.
Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has published an official install size in the sources available to us. Numbers are circulating anyway, and they come from leaks. Until the storefronts show a size on the pre-load page, plan for a large download and free up space rather than trusting any single figure.
A $79.99 standard edition is a premium price for a console game, and it shows how much confidence Take-Two has in this title. Publishers rarely push a price up on a game they expect to struggle. Setting the number at $79.99 is a bet that demand will absorb it.
That bet has consequences beyond this one title. If buyers pay $79.99 without visible resistance, other publishers will read the result as permission to move their own flagship prices up. If buyers balk, the next round of pricing decisions across the industry gets more cautious. Analysts and rival executives will watch pre-order momentum and launch-week chatter for exactly this signal.
